title: Wringer vacuity verdict
description: `vacuity.json` — what `wring verify --prove` found when it ran the same declared gates against the PRE-CHANGE tree. A SIBLING of manifest.json, like digests.json and untracked.json and for the same reason: `wringer.evidence.v1` is frozen, so this arrives as its own file and a reader that does not know it ignores it. The mechanism is a scratch worktree detached at HEAD, which IS the pre-change tree — tracked edits absent, untracked files naturally missing, no reverse-patching. A gate that passes on the changed tree and FAILS on the pre-change one tests this change; a gate that passes on both is insensitive to it. A lint gate passing on both is ordinary. EVERY required gate passing on both is the signal, and the verdict is `gates_vacuous`: the change ships with a green tick that proved nothing. Absent from any bundle whose run did not prove — every repo that has not opted in is unaffected, and `wring deliver` behaves for those exactly as it always has.

verdict.description: `proven` — at least one required gate failed on the pre-change tree, so the gates test this change. `gates_vacuous` — every required gate passed without it too. `not_applicable` — there was nothing to be vacuous about: an unchanged tree, or a required gate that failed the normal run, in which case the prove pass never runs at all (there is nothing to prove about a failure). `inconclusive` — the measurement could not be made honestly: the scratch worktree could not be created, or `run.prove_setup` failed, which would leave every pre-change gate failing on a broken environment rather than on the change. `inconclusive` is never `proven`, and it is never silently dropped.

reason.description: The verdict in a sentence, naming the gates it rests on. A refusal that only says no converts this feature into something people turn off.

worktree_ms.description: How long building the scratch worktree took. Recorded because ruling 3 refuses a configurable ceiling — every answer to 'what happens when you hit it' is worse than the cost, and skipping the pass would re-introduce the vacuity this feature exists to catch. So the cost is MEASURED instead, and a repo decides with numbers rather than guessing a threshold. There is no ceiling key in the config, here or anywhere.

prove_ms.description: How long the pre-change gates took, setup included. See `worktree_ms`.

setup.description: What `run.prove_setup` did in the scratch worktree, or null when the repo declared none. A detached worktree carries tracked files ONLY — no .venv, no node_modules, because those are gitignored — so in a repo whose dependencies are not committed every pre-change gate fails on a missing environment, and the comparison reads that as proof. That is a false `proven`, and it would fire on every run however tautological the tests. `run.prove_setup` is half of what closes it; a failing one yields `inconclusive`.

gates.description: One row per REQUIRED gate that ran on both trees. Optional gates are absent: they do not decide the outcome, so their sensitivity cannot make a green tick mean more or less than it did.

changed.description: How the gate did on the tree being verified.

pre_change.description: How the same gate did in the scratch worktree at HEAD.

sensitive.description: True when the gate passed on the changed tree and failed on the pre-change one — the shape that means it tests this change.

cites.description: One line saying WHY the pre-change gate failed, present exactly when `sensitive` is true — the other half of what closes the false-`proven` trap. A `sensitive` row means 'this failed without the change', and the reader has to be able to see whether that failure was the change or a missing environment: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yourproject'` is instantly legible as the latter. Deliberately NOT classified into environment-or-regression. Making the failure visible is the product; guessing at its meaning would be the cleverness this format exists to refuse.

pre_change_log.description: Bundle-relative path to the pre-change run's stdout, under `vacuity/`. Evidence, not summary: a reader who doubts a row can read both trees' output.
